sense: a woman: force or dishonour her

terms.gloss: violate, deflower (a girl); in general spoil, corrupt
evidence: Ter. Ad. 466–467: Fīliam ejus virginem vitiāvit.

terms.gloss: lie with (a woman), usually by force
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 28: nam eam compressit dē summō adulēscēns locō
terms.comment: Literally press, hold down. The usual word in the prologues of comedy for the rape, often at a night festival, from which the plot starts.

terms.gloss: dishonour by illicit sex: debauch, rape
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 36: quī illam stuprāvit noctū, Cereris vigiliīs
Cic. Fin. 2.66: Lucrētia vī stuprāta (Lewis & Short)

phrases.english: He violated his daughter, an unmarried girl.

phrases.latin: isque hīc compressit virginem, adulēscentulus, vī, vīnulentus multā nocte in viā
phrases.english: and here he forced a girl, a mere youth, by violence, drunk, late at night in the street

sources: Lewis & Short: vitio · Lewis & Short: comprimo · Lewis & Short: stupro
